title: The transported lax pushforward structure on sheafification generators
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal V$, two $\mathcal V$-small sites $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and a closed braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian category $\mathcal A$ relative to $\mathcal V$, with $\mathcal V$-small morphism sets. Use the canonical sheafified pointwise tensors and strong monoidal sheafification functors of [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators]. Write $a_C\dashv U_C$, $a_D\dashv U_D$ for sheafification and inclusion, $\eta_C,\eta_D$ for their units and $\epsilon_C,\epsilon_D$ for their counits. Write $t_C,t_D$ and $u_C,u_D$ for their tensor and unit generators. Let $E:C\to D$ be a functor such that restriction $r(P)=P\circ E^{\mathrm{op}}$ takes $K$-sheaves to $J$-sheaves, and let $R:\operatorname{Sh}(D,K;\mathcal A)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C,J;\mathcal A)$ be that restriction, so $U_CR=rU_D$. Give $U_D$ the lax structure right-adjoint to the strong structure on $a_D$ [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates]; give $r$ its pointwise strong monoidal structure; and give $R$ the lax structure transported from $a_CrU_D$ along the counit isomorphism $a_CU_CR\xrightarrow{\epsilon_C R}R$. Then its tensor and unit comparisons $\mu_R$ and $e_R$ satisfy, for every pair of sheaves $F,G$ on $D$,
$$
U_C(\mu_{R,F,G})\circ t_C(RF,RG)=r(t_D(F,G)),\qquad U_C(e_R)\circ u_C=r(u_D).
$$
Equivalently, the transported structure maps are the unique sheaf extensions of $r(t_D(F,G))$ and $r(u_D)$ along the actual sheafification units. No assertion that evaluation preserves sheaf tensor products is made.

source.place: Proof, second sentence; expanded identification of the transported lax structure. Project corroboration: WeilConjectures/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Monoidal.lean:170-207,375-393 and WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/Sites/PushforwardMonoidal.lean:85-114.

proof.text:
Use the canonical sheafified tensor of [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators]. We write composition right to left and suppress pointwise tensor subscripts. For either site write $a\dashv U$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Unpacking its canonical strong comparison, its inverse is
$$\delta_{P,Q}=a(\eta_P\otimes\eta_Q):a(P\otimes Q)\longrightarrow aP\otimes aQ=a(UaP\otimes UaQ),$$
and its unit comparison is $1_{a\underline{\mathbf1}}$; on sheaf morphisms the tensor is $f\otimes g=a(Uf\otimes Ug)$. By the mate construction [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates], the lax tensor of $U$ at $F,G$ is
$$m_{F,G}=U((\epsilon_F\otimes\epsilon_G)\delta_{UF,UG})\eta_{UF\otimes UG}.$$
The composite inside $U$ equals $a((U\epsilon_F\eta_{UF})\otimes(U\epsilon_G\eta_{UG}))=1$, by the two triangle identities. Therefore $m_{F,G}=\eta_{UF\otimes UG}=t(F,G)$. The mate of the identity unit comparison is $\eta_{\underline{\mathbf1}}=u$. This identifies the mate maps with the actual generators, for both sites.

source.place: Second sentence; normalization of the sheaf-inclusion mate maps.

proof.text:
Put $P=rU_DF=U_CRF$, $Q=rU_DG=U_CRG$, $H=R(F\otimes G)$ and $v=r(t_D(F,G)):P\otimes Q\to U_CH$. Restriction preserves the pointwise tensor and its unit componentwise, so its comparison maps are identities. Expand the composite lax structure and its transport along $\epsilon_CR:a_CU_CR\to R$:
$$\mu_{R,F,G}=\epsilon_{C,H}\,a_C(v)\,\mu^{a_C}_{P,Q}(\epsilon_{C,RF}^{-1}\otimes\epsilon_{C,RG}^{-1}).$$
Here step 1 supplies $m_D=t_D$. The counits are invertible because $U_C$ is a full inclusion [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; indeed the unique extension of $1_{U_CRF}$ is inverse to its counit, as both composites are identities by unique extension. The triangle identity gives $U_C(\epsilon_{C,RF}^{-1})=\eta_{C,P}$, and similarly for $G$. Consequently the tensor of these inverse counits is $a_C(\eta_{C,P}\otimes\eta_{C,Q})=\delta_{C,P,Q}$, which cancels $\mu^{a_C}_{P,Q}$. Thus
$$\mu_{R,F,G}=\epsilon_{C,H}a_C(v).$$
For the unit, put $H_0=R\mathbf1_D$ and $v_0=r(u_D):\underline{\mathbf1}\to U_CH_0$. The composite and transport unit formula directly gives $e_R=\epsilon_{C,H_0}a_C(v_0)$, since both the restriction and sheafification unit comparisons are identities.

source.place: Second sentence; explicit tensor and unit transport and cancellation.

proof.text:
For any presheaf map $w:S\to U_CH'$, naturality of the adjunction unit and the triangle identity give
$$U_C(\epsilon_{C,H'}a_C(w))\eta_{C,S}=U_C\epsilon_{C,H'}\,\eta_{C,U_CH'}w=w.$$
Apply this first with $S=P\otimes Q$, $H'=H$, $w=v$, and then with $S=\underline{\mathbf1}$, $H'=H_0$, $w=v_0$. By [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators], $t_C(RF,RG)=\eta_{C,P\otimes Q}$ and $u_C=\eta_{C,\underline{\mathbf1}}$. Inserting step 2 proves both displayed identities of the statement. This calculation is in presheaf Hom sets and uses no preservation of sheaf tensor products by evaluation.

source.place: Second sentence; generator equations from naturality and the triangle identity.

proof.text: Finally apply the two Hom bijections of [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators], on $C$, to the sheaf targets $R(F\otimes G)$ and $R\mathbf1_D$. The restricted generators are presheaf natural transformations, since restriction is precomposition. Each therefore has a unique sheaf extension, and step 3 identifies those extensions with $\mu_R$ and $e_R$. All objects involved are on the given $\mathcal V$-small sites and all morphism sets are in the fixed universe, as required by that lemma.

source.place: Second sentence; equivalence with unique sheaf extension.

proof_origin.place: Second sentence; explicit mate and counit calculation, corroborated by the project source listed in source.place.
